description:
This diagram illustrates the altitudinal zonation of vegetation and land cover on a mountain slope, progressing from high altitudes downwards.
1.  At the highest altitude, the dominant feature is "Bare rocks".
2.  Moving downslope, the next zone is characterised by "Grasses with bare soil", indicating a transition from barren rock to sparse vegetation.
3.  Further down, the vegetation becomes denser, forming "Alpine meadows", which are shown above a dashed horizontal line.
4.  This dashed line represents the "Tree line", marking the upper limit for tree growth.
5.  Below the tree line, the landscape transitions to "Mountain hay meadows", which appear more lush.
The diagram depicts a gradual change in vegetation type with decreasing altitude, culminating in an area with small houses, representing lower elevations or human settlement.
